title: Homology of a totalized cutoff cone equals smart vertical interval homology
statement: Let C be abelian, with totals for all nonnegative double complexes, and let K be one. Use the explicit cutoff tower of [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-tower-maps]. For any integer a, upper endpoint j in EInt with a<=j, and integer degree n, the homology of the cone of its a-to-j map is isomorphic to the homology of the extended total smart interval. For finite j=b this interval applies W[a,b) of [def-sp-double-complex-vertical-window] columnwise. At top it applies the smart lower truncation at a to the extended column and restricts back. At bottom it is zero (the inequality excludes this case).

proof.text: For finite upper endpoint b, the cone of tau_{<a} -> tau_{<b} in each column maps quasi-isomorphically to the quotient. The quotient maps quasi-isomorphically to tau_{>=a}(tau_{<b}). Smart truncations commute when a<=b, giving W[a,b). At top replace tau_{<b} by the original extended column. These comparisons are natural in the horizontal direction.
The unique tower maps are the totalizations of these columnwise smart inclusions, by their factorization into the monomorphic top inclusion.

Keep the column cones integer-indexed, including their possibly nonzero vertical degree -1; do not restrict them to nonnegative vertical degrees. Their uniform lower bound -1 still makes every total diagonal finite. Totalization commutes with cones after the standard sign change on the shifted summand. It preserves columnwise quasi-isomorphisms in this uniformly bounded-below situation: the cone has acyclic columns; eliminate successive horizontal components of a total cycle using vertical exactness. The vertical degree decreases, so the finite diagonal chase terminates. This is a kernel-image chase in an arbitrary abelian category. Apply homology to the resulting zigzag of quasi-isomorphisms. The cutoff and smart-window complexes have zero negative terms, so their extension-restriction loses no data. The cases a=b, negative bounds and negative homology degrees are included.
